newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Public Bank falls in heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: Public Bank falls in heavy volume.

text.p: Foreign shares in Malaysia's Public Bank traded over the counter in Singapore fell in heavy trading on Wednesday on talk that the company would soon allow foreigners to buy its local tranche shares, dealers said.
At 0733 GMT, the stock was down 17 cents at a new 1997 low of Singapore $2.36. Volume was more than 14.7 million shares.

"Apparently, there is circular going around that the company has proposed that foreigners be allowed to buy the local shares and get all the entitlements except voting rights," an institutional dealer with a local bank said.
Dealers said foreigner investors were dumping the stock with the premium between the local and foreign shares expected to disappear.
In Malaysia, the local tranche was trading at 3.54 ringgit, up 22 sen. The foreign tranche was down 38 sen to 4.04 ringgit.
